# Agent Policy Coverage and Attack Path

**Agent:** `support-agent (synthetic data)` · **Run:** `coverage-run-2026-10-24` · **Generated:** 2026-10-24T04:10:35Z

> Every value in this report is synthetic. It shows what three chart types add to a report: how a policy maps to risks, how an attack moves, and how several measurements compare at once.

## 1. Policy to risk mapping

Each curve joins a policy clause to a risk it addresses. Clauses and risks sit on one circle, grouped by policy section and risk category, and curves between groups are pulled together so shared routes read as bands. **A risk with no curve ending on it is not covered by any clause.** Here that is prompt injection.

**Figure: Policy clauses and the risks they address** (bundle)

| Source | Group | Target | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimize customer data | Policy: Data handling | PII leakage | Risk: Privacy |
| Minimize customer data | Policy: Data handling | Over-retention | Risk: Privacy |
| Redact PII in logs | Policy: Data handling | PII leakage | Risk: Privacy |
| Redact PII in logs | Policy: Data handling | Credential exfiltration | Risk: Security |
| 30-day retention | Policy: Data handling | Over-retention | Risk: Privacy |
| Least-privilege tools | Policy: Tool use | Tool misuse | Risk: Security |
| Least-privilege tools | Policy: Tool use | Credential exfiltration | Risk: Security |
| Approve payments | Policy: Tool use | Tool misuse | Risk: Security |
| Approve payments | Policy: Tool use | Unaccountable actions | Risk: Governance |
| No credential access | Policy: Tool use | Credential exfiltration | Risk: Security |
| Keep an audit trail | Policy: Oversight | Unaccountable actions | Risk: Governance |
| Escalate unsafe requests | Policy: Oversight | Harmful content | Risk: Safety |
| Escalate unsafe requests | Policy: Oversight | Deception | Risk: Safety |
| Refuse harmful requests | Policy: Content | Harmful content | Risk: Safety |
| Disclose AI identity | Policy: Content | Deception | Risk: Safety |

Not linked: Prompt injection.

## 2. Attack path

A prompt-injection attack that ends in credential exfiltration, with the controls that interrupt it. Arrows point from an attack step to the next step, or to the risk it realizes; a control points at the step it blocks. The layout is computed from the links, so position carries no meaning: follow the arrows.

**Figure: Attack flow and the controls that interrupt it** (graph)

| Source | Group | Target | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plant instruction in web page | Attack step | Agent follows planted text | Attack step |
| Agent follows planted text | Attack step | Agent runs shell tool | Attack step |
| Agent runs shell tool | Attack step | Read environment credentials | Attack step |
| Read environment credentials | Attack step | Send to attacker URL | Attack step |
| Agent follows planted text | Attack step | Prompt injection | Risk |
| Send to attacker URL | Attack step | Credential exfiltration | Risk |
| Input filter | Control | Agent follows planted text | Attack step |
| Sandbox without env vars | Control | Read environment credentials | Attack step |
| Egress allowlist | Control | Send to attacker URL | Attack step |

## 3. What each defense buys

Each line is one agent configuration and each vertical axis is one measurement on its own scale. Axes where lower is better are flipped, so a line near the top is good on every axis. The sandbox run has no latency measurement: its line stops at the previous axis and is not drawn through zero.

**Figure: Four agent configurations across five measurements** (parallel)

| Config | Task utility | Attack success rate (lower is better) | Policy coverage | False refusals (lower is better) | Latency p95 (lower is better) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 94% | 33% | 40% | 2% | 4.1 |
| Input filter | 91% | 18% | 55% | 7% | 4.6 |
| Sandbox | 93% | 12% | 60% | 3% | N/A |
| Filter and sandbox | 89% | 4% | 85% | 8% | 5.2 |
